data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["binary majority with 3 neighbors is a tie-free rule, unlike Ising at even degree where ties complicate fixation","random 3-regular graphs are locally tree-like, not lattices, so no geometry-driven coarsening length scale"],"overturn_conditions":["if rigorous results show whp consensus on random d-regular graphs for majority dynamics, the analogy-based claim dies","if the matching-collapse event has probability bounded away from 1, the transfer fails"],"shared_structure":["energy (monochromatic edge count) non-decreasing under local majority updates, exactly like Ising energy at zero temperature","expanding underlying graph preventing curvature-driven interface shrinkage to zero","absorption at local energy maxima = locally stable configurations"],"source_memory_refs":["zero-temperature Glauber/Ising coarsening on expanders: fixation in non-consensus configurations occurs with high probability on random regular graphs"],"transfer_claims":["as on expanders, coarsening fixes at a mixed configuration whp because linear interface cannot fully vanish before matching-collapse"]},"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0. The obstruction structures are exactly the locally stable mixed configurations in which every vertex has at least two same-color neighbors, i.e. the cut's crossing edges form a matching and every monochromatic component is an induced subgraph of minimum degree >= 2 containing a cycle. The dynamics is absorbed by the first such configuration it meets; since each majority update strictly increases the count of monochromatic edges, absorption happens after O(n log n) updates, and the density of stable mixed configurations among the energy landscape is positive. The expected count of reachable trapping configurations is Theta(exp(c n)) with c approx 0.07-0.1, while each traps a basin of size exp(Theta(n)) covering in total a 1-o(1) fraction of initial colorings; hence consensus probability is exp(-Theta(n)) -> 0.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the coarsening process on expanders in fact eliminates all interface whp (contradicting the expander-fixation analogy), consensus probability would tend to 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If matching-cut traps have basins of total measure exp(-Theta(n)) only, the conclusion fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the interface cannot collapse to a matching because expanding geometry keeps interface length linear at freezing time, traps could instead be non-stable frozen-looking states \u2014 but on a finite graph absorption must still be at a stable state, and the characterization of stable states is exact.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Define energy = number of monochromatic edges; asynchronous majority updates never decrease it and each unstable vertex update strictly increases it. Absorption therefore occurs at a local maximum. Local maxima are cuts where crossing edges form a matching: any vertex with two opposite-color neighbors is unstable, so stability forces at most one crossing edge per vertex, i.e. a matching cut. Such cuts decompose the graph into two induced subgraphs of minimum degree >= 2, hence each color class is a union of components containing cycles. On a random 3-regular graph one constructs exponentially many matching cuts by taking two disjoint induced subgraphs of girth >= 4 (e.g. unions of cycles in the cycle space) and matching their boundaries; the cycle space has dimension n/2 + 1, giving at least 2^{c n} cuts. But the key objection (SRC_011) is that counting obstructions is not counting the consensus event, since the initial coloring is not itself stable. The answer is basin analysis: from a random coloring, the update process is a low-temperature coarsening similar to zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on the 3-regular lattice; coarsening on non-amenable (expanding) graphs does not coarsen to consensus because expansion maintains O(n) interface length, and the dynamics freezes when the interface collapses to a matching \u2014 an event that happens with probability 1 - exp(-Theta(n)). This mirrors the proven behaviour of zero-temperature Ising dynamics on expanders (e.g. random regular graphs), where fixation at a non-consensus configuration occurs whp.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
